sounds.how: Lay the flat front part of the tongue against the roof of the mouth, just behind the ridge. The tip is not what touches. Then let go, as for t.
sounds.slip: Two sounds, t and then y. It is one sound, made in one place.
sounds.writing: Before e and i the letters d, t, n and l are usually said soft with no mark: ticho, deti. Some words keep them hard, such as ten, teraz and borrowed words like telefón.

sounds.how: The same place as ť: the flat front part of the tongue on the roof of the mouth, just behind the ridge. Add your voice.
sounds.slip: The j of English "jam", or d and then y. Keep it one short, soft d.
sounds.writing: Before e and i the letters d, t, n and l are usually said soft with no mark: deti, divadlo. Some words keep them hard, such as ten, teraz and borrowed words like telefón.

sounds.how: The flat front part of the tongue lies on the roof of the mouth, as for ť, and the air goes out through the nose. It is the ñ of Spanish "señor".
sounds.slip: Two sounds, n and then y. It is one sound.
sounds.writing: Before e and i the letters d, t, n and l are usually said soft with no mark: nie, nič. Some words keep them hard, such as ten, teraz and borrowed words like telefón.

sounds.how: Put the tip of the tongue on the ridge, as for l, and lift the middle of the tongue toward the roof of the mouth. It sounds lighter and softer than l.
sounds.slip: A plain l. Before e and i most Slovaks say it that way too, and in the west before every vowel, and are understood.

sounds.how: The mouth is the same as for a. Hold the vowel about twice as long.
sounds.slip: Saying it short. Length changes the word: pas is a passport, pás is a belt.

sounds.how: The mouth is the same as for e. Hold the vowel about twice as long, without sliding toward i.
sounds.slip: The ay of English "say". The sound stays the same from start to end.

sounds.how: The mouth is the same as for i. Hold the vowel about twice as long. The letters y and ý sound the same as i and í.
sounds.slip: Saying it short, as in English "win".

sounds.how: The mouth is the same as for o. Hold the vowel about twice as long. It is found mostly in borrowed words.
sounds.slip: The o of English "go", which slides toward u. The sound stays the same from start to end.

sounds.how: The mouth is the same as for u: lips rounded, tongue pulled back. Hold the vowel about twice as long.
sounds.slip: Saying it short. Length changes the word: sud is a barrel, súd is a court.

sounds.how: Start with the rounded lips of a very short u and glide at once into o. Both parts are one syllable: stuol.
sounds.slip: A plain long o, or the o of English "go".

sounds.how: Start with a very short i, like the y of English "yes", and glide at once into a. Both parts are one syllable.
sounds.slip: Two syllables, pi-a-tok. The word has two: pia-tok.

sounds.how: Start with a very short i, like the y of English "yes", and glide at once into e. Both parts are one syllable.
sounds.slip: Two syllables, bi-e-ly. The word has two: bie-ly.

sounds.how: Start with a very short i, like the y of English "yes", and glide at once into u. It is found only in a few endings.
sounds.slip: Two syllables, i and then u.

sounds.how: Most Slovaks say it exactly like e. In careful, formal speech the mouth opens a little more, toward the a of English "cat".
sounds.slip: Saying it like a. It is written only after b, p, m and v.

sounds.how: Rest the tip of the tongue loosely on the ridge behind the upper teeth and let the air make it tap there, once or twice.
sounds.slip: The English r, where the tongue touches nothing. Here the tip has to touch the ridge.

sounds.how: In a word like krk the r is the vowel of its syllable. A long ŕ is the same, with the tip of the tongue tapping about twice as long and no vowel before or after it.
sounds.slip: Slipping in a vowel: ver-ba. The syllable is the r alone.

sounds.how: In a word like vlk the l is the vowel of its syllable. A long ĺ is the same: keep the tip of the tongue on the ridge about twice as long, with no vowel before or after it.
sounds.slip: Slipping in a vowel: stulp or stelp. The syllable is the l alone.

sounds.how: Lift the back of the tongue close to the soft back part of the roof of the mouth, as for k, but leave a small gap. The air rubs through it. It is the ch of Scottish "loch".
sounds.slip: A k, where the air stops, or the ch of English "cheese".

sounds.how: It is made in the throat, with the tongue at rest, and the voice hums through it. Put a hand on your throat: you feel it buzz.
sounds.slip: The English h, which is only breath, or ch.

sounds.how: Before a vowel the lower lip touches the upper teeth lightly, with less buzz than English v. At the end of a syllable it turns into a short u: pravda sounds like prauda.
sounds.slip: A full v at the end of a syllable: domov ends like domou. At the start of a word before a sound with no voice it is said f: vták.

sounds.how: One sound: the tip of the tongue closes on the ridge behind the upper teeth, as for d, and opens into z. It is the ds of English "kids".
sounds.slip: Two sounds with a break between them, d and then z.

sounds.how: One sound: the tip of the tongue closes just behind the ridge and opens into ž. It sounds a little harder than the j of English "jam".
sounds.slip: Two sounds with a break between them, d and then ž.

sounds.how: One sound: the tongue closes on the ridge behind the upper teeth, as for t, and opens into s. It is the ts of English "cats".
sounds.slip: A k or an s, as the letter c is read in English. In Slovak c is always ts.

sounds.how: p, t and k are said without the puff of air they have at the start of an English word. Hold a hand in front of your mouth: you should feel almost nothing.
sounds.slip: The breathy p, t and k of English "pen", "ten" and "ken".
